page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-16 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine profile engineered for memory-intensive workloads. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 248.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. This extreme memory density is designed to handle footprints that exceed conventional compute configurations without demanding excess processing threads.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent block volumes for all file system and persistent data needs. Accelerated processing hardware is absent, as the system provides zero GPUs. Additionally, it allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking structures or configured routing gateways for outbound and inbound connectivity.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the m4-hypermem-16 provides a focused operational profile by packaging vast physical memory alongside a modest processing footprint. Deployments that require substantial memory capacity avoid paying for unneeded vCPUs. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include enterprise in-memory databases, large cache layers, memory-bound analytics engines, and in-memory transactional processing environments.
